speaker: Doctor
text:
The ultrasound indicates a well-circumscribed, cystic lesion in the subcutaneous tissue, which is inconsistent with pneumonia; do you have any history of trauma, skin infections, or recent dental issues in that area?

REQUEST TEST: CEA, CA 19-9, CA 125.
REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_MRI.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CEA: NORMAL READINGS; CA 19-9: NORMAL READINGS; CA 125: NORMAL READINGS; Neck_MRI: Well-circumscribed lesion in the subcutaneous tissue confirming the cystic nature observed on ultrasound, with no evidence of malignancy or extension into surrounding structures.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the normal tumor markers and MRI confirming a benign, cystic nature of the lesion, I need to determine the specific fluid content and origin. Do you have a history of a congenital pituitary cyst or any thyroid nodules that might suggest a thyroglossal duct cyst?

REQUEST TEST: Fine_Needle_Aspiration.
REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_MRI_Enhanced.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fine_Needle_Aspiration: Fluid aspirated consistent with serous content; no malignant cells identified. Neck_MRI_Enhanced: Well-circumscribed cystic lesion with thin wall and no internal enhancement, confirming benign cystic nature without solid components or vascularity suggestive of neoplasm.

speaker: Doctor
text: The aspiration of serous fluid and MRI findings confirm a benign, non-thyroidal cystic lesion in the subcutaneous tissue. Given the location and imaging characteristics, do you have any history of a midline neck mass that moves when you protrude your tongue?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Branchial Cleft Cyst. The patient's history of a midline mass moving with tongue protrusion was denied in the most recent input; instead, the swelling is located on the nape of the neck. Given the cystic nature confirmed by ultrasound, MRI, and serous fluid aspiration, along with the location and lack of malignancy, this is most consistent with a branchial cleft cyst.
